concept: ERS exception for selective range predicates
summary: Source-anchored research for ERS exception for selective range predicates. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: The selective-range exception changes only the order of the Range and Sort keys: keep Equality fields first, then use ERS when the range narrows results enough to make sorting the smaller set worthwhile; otherwise favor ESR when avoiding an in-memory sort matters. (high confidence)

When a very selective range key is placed before the sort key (ERS), the query needs an in-memory sort, which reduces the number of documents to sort. Placing the range after the sort (ESR) avoids the in-memory sort. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes/

MongoDB's manual describes the ERS condition qualitatively, as a range predicate that is 'very selective', and sets no numeric cutoff on this page. It tells you to choose between sort-before-range and range-before-sort based on your index's specific needs, so assess the tradeoff on representative data instead of treating ERS as a fixed selectivity threshold. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline/

In one synthetic 200,000-order example, for total >= 499, the ESR index scanned 2,338 keys to return one order while the ERS index scanned one key and sorted that one result; this illustrates a possible ERS win, not a portable performance ratio. (low confidence) (verified as of 2023-07-09)
